observed_result: Four sources have a real execution path and each matches its hand-computed table. (1) ExternalTimeline{ChannelCount: 2} with the declared entries (0,0,0.5), (0,1,1.25), (2,1,2) and (3,0,0) released step 0 -> [0.5, 1.25], step 1 -> [0, 0], step 2 -> [0, 2], step 3 -> [0, 0] and step 9 -> [0, 0]: a step with no entry releases zero, and a step past the last entry is zero rather than an error. Releasing twice returns the same row and leaves the declared entries untouched. Eight invalid declarations are refused: no channel, a step that goes backwards, a channel at or above the count, a negative channel, a negative rate, +Inf, NaN, and the same step and channel declared twice. (2) NeuralActivity{Set: alpn, Gain: 0.5, Channel: 1} over the resolved set {1,2} of the three-neuron annotated fixture released activity [10, 0.25, 0.75] -> mean 0.5 -> [0, 0.25]; activity [10, -1, -3] -> mean -2, times 0.5 = -1 -> clamped to [0, 0]; activity [10, 0, 4] -> mean 2 -> [0, 1]. Node 0 is outside the set and its large value changed nothing, which is the point of requiring an explicit set. Seven refusals: no activity, activity shorter than the largest node index, non-finite activity, an unresolved (zero value) set, a set that resolved to no node, a non-finite gain and a negative channel. The set cannot be forged: simulate.ResolvedSet keeps its indices private and the new simulate.ResolvedSet.Nodes accessor returns an ascending owned copy, so the test resolves a real graph. (3) InternalResource{Resource: 'energy', Coefficient: 2, Threshold: 0.25} follows the declared rule Coefficient * max(amount - Threshold, 0): energy 1.25 -> [2], 0.75 -> [1], 0.25 -> [0], 0.1 -> [0], never a negative value. It refuses a missing resource map, a map without the named resource, a non-finite amount, an unnamed resource, a negative or non-finite coefficient, a non-finite threshold and a negative channel. (4) Replay{Trace: [[0,1.5],[2,0],[0.25,0.25]]} returned step 0 -> [0, 1.5], step 1 -> [2, 0], step 2 -> [0.25, 0.25] and refused step 3, the end of the recording. The returned row is a copy: overwriting all three handed-out rows left the stored trace unchanged. Replay has exactly one field, Trace [][]float64, and exactly two methods, Channels and Release (checked by reflection), so it holds no reader, path, clock or client and cannot fetch anything from outside the recording. An empty trace, an empty row, a ragged trace, a negative value and a non-finite value are refused. Every source re-checks feedback against its own step even though the caller filtered it: with feedback available only at step 3 offered at step 2, all four refuse, and so they do for feedback on another clock (milliseconds against the model-step clock) and for an invalid feedback value. Every release is finite, non-negative (negative zero included: the shared gate stores a positive zero) and exactly Channels() values wide, with and without an observation in the context. The trainable controller is reserved by name only: NewController returns nil and ErrControllerNotImplemented. The race detector reports nothing.
assumption_statement: Fixture only: a three-neuron annotated graph and hand-declared contexts, with no biological claim about which neurons modulate what. The named set of a neural source is always the researcher's declaration; nothing here infers that an unknown neuron is modulatory. This ticket covers the first layer only, source -> non-negative release rate per channel; no concentration, diffusion, decay or receptor is modelled. A release step is counted on the model-step clock (modulation.ReleaseTimeUnit = signal.TimeUnitModelStep), so feedback offered to a source must carry that unit; other units are rejected rather than converted. NeuralActivity and InternalResource report Channels() as Channel+1, so a source that drives channel k returns a k+1 wide vector whose lower channels release zero.
